sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Importing data types
sections.what: Brings in the data shapes for tasks, habits, routines, focus sessions, assignments, internships, hackathons, projects and goals.
sections.why: Likely reason: the calculations need to know each item's fields.

sections.name: getTodayDateString (part 1)
sections.title: Today's date and the momentum score
sections.what: Gets today's date as text, then calculates a momentum score from 0 to 100 using today's tasks, active habits, routines and focus minutes, each with a set weight.
sections.why: Likely reason: one score summarizes how the day is going. The weights are set in the code, and their reason is not stated.
sections.watch_out: Today's date uses UTC, so the count of today's tasks can be off for users far from UTC near midnight.

sections.name: getTodayDateString: if
sections.title: Life score returns zero when there is no data
sections.what: If there are no habits, tasks, goals or focus sessions at all, the life score is zero. Otherwise it blends habit success, task completion, goal progress and focus hours, capped between 0 and 100.
sections.why: Likely reason: an empty account should show zero, not a misleading score.
sections.watch_out: The focus hours target of 30 hours is a fixed number, not a user setting.

sections.name: AnalyticsAggregate (part 1)
sections.title: Building the aggregate analytics values
sections.what: Computes task and assignment completion rates, average habit success, focus hours, average project progress and an activity flag. Also calls the momentum score with routines left empty.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: gathers the dashboard numbers in one step.
sections.watch_out: Passing routines as an empty list means the routine part of the momentum score is always zero.

sections.name: AnalyticsAggregate (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the aggregate values
sections.what: Returns the analytics object. Monthly and yearly scores are the weekly score scaled down. Study hours, goal average, coding hours, water intake and sleep are fixed at zero, and mood is a fixed text label.
sections.why: Likely reason: some metrics are not tracked yet, so they show as placeholders.
sections.watch_out: Internships applied is just the total number of internship entries, not a count of applications sent.

sections.name: exportToCSV
sections.title: Exporting rows as a CSV download
sections.what: Turns a list of rows into comma separated text with a header row taken from the first row's fields, wraps cells that contain commas or quotes, then starts a browser download with the given file name.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the user take their data into a spreadsheet.
sections.watch_out: Only the first row's fields become columns, so any extra fields in later rows are dropped silently. The download needs a browser, so it will not run on a server.

summary: Turns raw task, habit, focus and goal data into scores and totals for the dashboard, and exports rows as a CSV file download.
purpose: Provide the momentum score, life score, aggregate analytics, and a CSV export.
why: Likely reason: keeps the score arithmetic out of the screens. Reason not stated beyond that.
how: 1. Gets today's date as text. 2. Momentum score: today's tasks count 35 percent, habits 35, routines 15 and focus 15. 3. Life score: habits count 30 percent, tasks 25, goals 25 and focus 20, with focus measured against 30 hours. 4. Aggregate: computes rates and totals, then derives monthly and yearly scores from the weekly one. 5. CSV export: writes a header row and quoted rows, then starts a browser download.
inputs: Lists of tasks, habits, routines, focus sessions, goals, assignments, internships, hackathons and projects, and a list of rows to export.
outputs: Numbers from 0 to 100, an aggregate analytics object, and a CSV file download in the browser.
risks: Today's date comes from UTC, so near midnight the day can differ from the user's local day. Routines are always passed in empty, so the momentum score can reach at most 85. Several aggregate fields are fixed at zero or fixed text. Monthly and yearly scores are scaled guesses, not real history.
debug: If the momentum score never passes 85, the empty routines input is the cause, not the data. If today's numbers look off, compare the UTC date with the local date. For CSV problems, check the columns of the first row, since only those become headers.
